comments.body:
Hi there. I can relate to what you are saying, I begun in EPFL and then changed to do the AEAI in Fribourg. As somebody said, you can work in Swiss office if you do the ETH/EPFL or if you do an high school like in Basel, Fribourg (my case), Geneva, Mendrisio or Bern (Geneva and Bern aren't that great IMO). Nowadays the high school got really great teacher and more focus on "Swiss architecture" that will be really helpfull when you will do your first competition in an office. 

Back in my days (I finish my master in Fribourg in 2013) there had a really cool vibe in my year. Don't get me wrong, you will work sooooooo much in order to finish your project, but suffering with your classroom (maybe 80 people the first year) will do a strong feeling of solidarity. Because, let be honest, you will be at least one time eaten alive in front of the all class and it's kind of tough! I was born in Fribourg so language was not an issue for me but some foreigner people there were accepted as other without any problems.

Only problem if you choose this path, you have to do 1year of pratcice in a Swiss office. You can send portfolio if you want to try that. I actually have a small office (we won 2 competition in 2022, sadly just one is under construction), so high school can be as good as ETH/EPFL in my opinion.

You have to be strong in order to do this kind of study, but architecte is a great job in the end, especially if you can express yourself trough competition.

Sorry for my rusty english, it's well known than architecte are not great at other language!
comments.author: Giggs1986
